title: A liquid column at rest under gravity: hydrostatic pressure and a surface that stays
source: Hydrostatics: p = ρ g (h − z) below a free surface at height h at the gauge pressure 0; the liquid holds still

quantities.quantity: gauge pressure at the lowest cell centre, ρ g (h − Δx/2)
quantities.reason: the weakly compressible lattice's density grows by 0.6 % down the column, and the pressure in the cells against the surface is read a cell away from it (measured 0.67 % of ρ g h at worst over the column)

quantities.quantity: the liquid's upper extent at the end, h
quantities.reason: the top cell stays at least half full (the column stands 0.3 % lower by its compression), so the extent is the face above it exactly

quantities.quantity: the largest speed at the end (zero: the liquid holds still)
quantities.reason: spurious currents at the interface cells: measured 8.5·10⁻⁴ m/s, 2.7·10⁻⁴ of the free-fall speed √(2 g h)
the mass exchange is exact; round-off over 4000 steps (measured 4·10⁻¹³)
